narrative.overview: The shortest assembly manual ever printed: one part, two steps. A white sheet ruled into panels by 3px ink lines; Elixir purple owns the cover, WebAssembly blue marks the one file and every active state; wordless pictograms, circled numerals at impact scale, an exploded drawing of the file.
keyCharacteristics: WebAssembly blue for the file and active states
Circled step numerals at impact scale
Exploded ink drawing with dashed leaders

rules.name: The Two-Worlds Rule
rules.body: Purple is Elixir, blue is WebAssembly; the page uses exactly these two hues at page scale and no third accent. Purple fills a region; blue marks the file you ship and things you can act on.

rules.name: The Positive Rule
rules.body: Nothing is crossed out, compared or put down. Limits are stated plainly in Before you start, next to what works.

dos: Use Elixir purple as a field and WebAssembly blue for the file and active states.
Keep step numerals the largest marks after the name.
Draw new figures in the pictogram grammar: uniform round-capped strokes, ink on white, one blue accent at most.
Keep every number to PRODUCT.md's evidence.
donts: Don't cross out, compare or disparage other tools.
Don't add a third accent, gradients, glows or card shadows.
Don't put a small label above a heading.
Don't use a dark terminal hero or a grid of icon cards.
Don't shade or put perspective on pictograms.
